newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks end mixed as Dow edges to modest gain.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks end mixed as Dow edges to modest gain.

text.p: Wall Street stocks turned in a mixed performance on Monday, with the Dow industrials scratching out marginal gains and tech stocks falling ahead of the first of a barrage of key reports on the U.S. economy.
The Dow rose eight points to close unofficially at 8121, barely topping its previous record closing high of 8116.93, set on July 24.
Cyclical stocks fared best during the session, a sign that portfolio managers were aligning their holdings in anticipation of strong economic data, analysts said.
Among the strongest Dow gainers on the session were Aluminum Co of America, Sears, Roebuck and Co and General Motors Corp, all cyclicals.
GM, which rose 1-5/8 to 58-1/2, also benefited from quick resolutions to strikes at company plants in Ontario and Michigan, analysts said.
Notably absent from the advance were technology stocks, which ended generally lower. While techs share some of the cyclical sector's characteristics, recent underperformance was not one of those.
"There are some real value worries in the techs, especially if you look at the computer makers," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany.
"Some of them are trading at price-to-earnings ratios that are at their highest in six years," he said.

Such concerns prompted one analyst, Andrew Neff at Bear Stearns, to cut his rating on high-flyer Dell Computer Corp to accumulate from buy. Shares in Dell fell 2-5/8 to 78-7/8 in the first trading after its two-for-one stock split.
The pressure spread through the personal computer group, pulling Compaq Computer Corp down 3-1/8 to 132-1/2 and International Business Machines Corp off two to 105.

Investors will receive a significant reading on the economy Tuesday morning, with release of the second-quarter employment cost index. The index is watched closely for its comprehensive review of labor costs, including benefits.
Economists expect the index to show an increase of 0.8 percent, up from 0.6 percent in the first quarter.
Among individual issues, Donna Karan International Inc climbed 1-5/16 to 11-3/4.
The company named longtime Polo Ralph Lauren Corp executive John Idol as its chief executive, charging him with restoring the company to profitability.
Freeport-McMoRan Inc gained 4-5/8 to 31-3/16 after announcing it would merge with IMC Global Inc in a stock-swap deal. IMC shares fell 5/8 to 33-1/8.

Owens-Illinois Inc rose 3-5/8 to 34-13/16 and Progressive Corp climbed 2-1/2 to 101-15/16. The companies were added to the Standard & Poor's 500 index, the benchmark for many mutual funds based on indices.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 6.05 points to 1563.53.
